scoring_justification: Compare agent-reported numeric quantities to paper gold with tolerances; recompute from raw is infeasible because the raw DFT artifacts (charge densities, wavefunctions) are too large and tool-specific to recompute in the verifier sandbox. The paper-reported results are the target.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold values and tolerances for all scored artifacts
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Extracted from the paper: total magnetic moment 2.02 μB, C-2p 0.85 μB, Zn 0.11 μB, O 0.05 μB, formation energy 5.3 eV, C-2s peak -9 eV, C-2p peak 2.3 eV, coupling energy 63 meV (0.063 eV), non-magnetic threshold ≤0.01 μB. All from Fig.1 and body text.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Direct extraction from the paper's reported numbers; reference solve.sh writes these exact values.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the actual published DFT results for carbon-doped ZnO; they serve as the reproduction target.

outputs.description: Magnetic moment per supercell for C_Zn and C_I defects. The paper reports these configurations as non-magnetic. The checker verifies that each moment is ≤ 0.01 μ_B.
Energy positions of the carbon 2s and 2p peaks in the local density of states of the C_O defect, relative to the Fermi level.
Total magnetic moment per carbon, orbital-resolved contributions, and formation energy of the substitutional C_O defect.
Energy difference between the antiferromagnetic and ferromagnetic spin alignments of two C_O defects. A positive value indicates a ferromagnetic ground state.

output_contract.notes: All numeric quantities are compared against the paper-reported values with tolerances appropriate for a DFT reimplementation using an open-source code and a different pseudopotential set. The load-bearing steps 05 and 07 ensure that the intermediate DFT pipeline must be executed to produce the target properties.

steps.description: Check that C_Zn and C_I moments are <= 0.01 μ_B (non-magnetic).
LDOS peak positions relative to Fermi level.
Total magnetic moment, orbital contributions, and formation energy of C_O defect.
FM-AFM energy difference for two C_O defects.
